reason: PATO_0001891 'ovate' is a 3-D shape ('spheroid ... egg-shaped'), with 'egg-shaped' as an exact synonym. That is exactly what oviform means for bulbs and fruits. The flat outline is the separate FLOPO_0991024, so the first check mixed up the two classes.

In the one source flora (FNA sedges), 'flagged' leaves have a blade, as opposed to 'bladeless' sheaths, so 'leaf lamina present' is right for leaves. Elsewhere 'flagged' (flag petal, flag leaf) means something else, so only use it when the bearer is a leaf.

Axillary bulblets are bulbils, the above-ground offsets in the axils. That matches R3168/R3169 and 'without proliferous bulbils' (R2145, bulbil absent). PO bulb is the underground storage organ, so asserting its absence is wrong. The rule stays entity_absence.
This matches the accepted rule 'summer-green' → PATO_0001731 deciduous (plant) (R1236). As a plant-level habit, green only during the growing season is the opposite of evergreen (plant).

Frutescent habit (FLOPO_0987002) is already a habit value that belongs to the whole plant, like 'shrublike' (R1491), which has no constraint. 'Somewhat or small-shrubby' is a degree, not a new quality. A constraint adds nothing.
The text only denies a central bundle of paraphyses. 'Paraphysis absent' claims there are none at all, and paraphyses may still sit among the sporangia. No existing class says this correctly.

This follows the accepted rules 'dichotomous' (C199) and 'dichotomously forked' (R0431) → PATO_0001784 bifurcated. Repeated forking is the same forking quality, and there is no PATO or FLOPO term for repeated forking.
The core hue is a pale brown. The grayish and straw tints are finer detail than PATO's colour terms, and there is no closer existing class (straw yellow PATO_0104343 is yellow, not brown).

The quality is a surface with fine lines (striated). 'Palmately' only says how the lines are arranged, and no palmately striate class exists. The palmate leaf-division classes (FLOPO_0991158, 0991282) are about lobing, not lines.
An exact existing FLOPO class (a child of PATO scaly) covers small peltate scales with star-like radiating arms.
Subcoriaceous is defined as somewhat leathery, thinner or less rigid than coriaceous. That is what 'thinly leathery' says.

In a hyphenated indumentum term the last word names the main type ('woolly' = lanate, an exact synonym). This follows R1995 'velvety-tomentose' → one value. 'Cobwebby' only says the wool is thin and loose, and arachnose (PATO_0002344) would lose the woolly part.
'Felted' is an exact synonym of PATO pannose and is the main word. 'Cobwebby' only describes how thin the felt is. Same reasoning as R2213.
PO_0006321 has 'primary inflorescence branch' as a synonym, so the rule is right inside an inflorescence. A vegetative primary branch should go to branch (PO_0025073).
Plural of R2233; same constraint.
French form of R2233; only correct inside an inflorescence.
FLOPO already has an involucre lobe class, so the earlier reason ('no involucre lobe class') is out of date. A lobe of a fused involucre is not a free involucral bract.
Plural of R2241; same existing class.
Variant of R2241; same existing class.

The meaning depends on the plant family. 'Floral tube' is the hypanthium in Onagraceae, Lythraceae and Thymelaeaceae, but the perianth tube (FLOPO_0986010) in Iridaceae, Amaryllidaceae and others. A part-name constraint cannot express a family, so a bare rule would mislabel one group either way.

Generic 'anther appendage' can be a connective appendage (FLOPO_0986073) or a theca appendage such as the awns and spurs in Ericaceae (FLOPO_0986131); both classes exist. Mapping to the connective is wrong for the theca kind. Mapping to the anther would wrongly give the anther the appendage's size or shape.
Plural of R2255; same ambiguity between connective appendage and theca appendage.

An apical anther appendage is the extension of the connective beyond the thecae (Asteraceae, Melastomataceae). Theca appendages (spurs, awns) are dorsal or basal, not apical. The bearer is the appendage, not the whole connective.
French generic form of R2255; ambiguous between connective appendage and theca appendage.

A member of an undifferentiated perianth is what PO calls a tepal, and the floras use 'perianth parts' mainly for such flowers. Where calyx and corolla are distinct, the text names a sepal or petal. 'Floral organ' would also cover stamens and carpels, which is too broad.
Plural of R2259; same reasoning.
French equivalent of R2259; same reasoning.
French plural of R2259; same reasoning.
Same as R2259: a perianth member of an undifferentiated perianth is a tepal, and floral organ is too broad.

'Bloom' as a part name is ambiguous (flowers or flowering versus a waxy coat). The waxy sense is already covered by the quality rule 'bloom' → glaucous (R0960, as for pruinose C222), which keeps the organ as the bearer.
